newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA CHEMICAL PLANT RAISES EXPORT REVENUE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA CHEMICAL PLANT RAISES EXPORT REVENUE.

text.p: Bulgaria's Himko chemical plant, which is offered for partial privatisation, raised revenue from export sales for the first nine months of 1996 by $10 million to $107 million over the same period last year, an official said on Thursday.

In lev terms, pre-tax profit doubled to 7.3 billion levs for the same period but the currency has fallen from 70 to the dollar at the beginning of the year to about 216 now. The plant exports 92 percent of its products.
Himko's net profit for 1994 was 60 million levs.

A Himko senior official, who declined to be named, said the ratza-based chemical plant had produced some 400 tonnes of ammonia, more than 580 tonnes of carbamide, some 9,000 tonnes of carbon sulphide and more than two million metres of argon.
The Privatisation Agency has put on the counter 60 percent of Himko, which is Bulgaria's second chemical giant after calcinated soda producer Sodi-Devnya.
The plant is among 20 major state enterprises which the government hopes to sell by year-end in a bid to raise desperately needed cash.
The plant, which imports 64 percent of its raw materials, has 20 installations, including for reforming, carbamide, carbon sulphide, carbon dioxide and a catalytic installation.

Earlier this year Himko set up a joint venture with Frankfurt-based Messer Grieshelm GmbH, a subsidiary of Germany's Hoechst , to distribute industrial gases in the region. Himko has 49 percent and the Germans have the remaining stake.
